name: Abuna’s Guard

abilities.name: Sea Sickness
abilities.text: As these men are inexperienced sailors. Caught up in sea combat, they suffer various penalties.

abilities.name: Svinfylking
abilities.text: The unit moves into a boar-shaped attack formation.\\n

abilities.name: Steady
abilities.text: Improves the unit's ability to defend at the cost of their mobility.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Encourage
attributes.text: This unit provides a morale bonus to nearby allies.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: Our father must be protected from the heathen hordes who seek his end.
history: As the desert kingdoms abandoned polytheism, religious figures emerged who became powerful, not only within their faiths, but also within political circles. For instance, Frumentius, a Tyrene slave who went on to become the first Bishop of Aksum, influenced the politics of the region even before he was ordained. As a civil servant, he first converted King Ezana to Christianity and later was regent to the Aksumite crown prince after Ezana's death. During this time he granted Christians religious freedom and, after being ordained and establishing a Holy See, became known as "Abuna" ("Our Father") amongst his congregation. Such was Frumentius' renown and importance to Aksumite politics, future kings refused Roman requests to replace him with someone they felt would better serve Imperial interests.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
